{{Short description|Complex-valued mathematical sequence}}
A '''Zadoff–Chu (ZC) sequence''' <ref name="Zepernick">{{cite book |last1=Zepernick |first1=Hans-Jürgen |last2=Finger |first2=Adolf |title=Pseudo Random Signal Processing: Theory and Application |date=2005 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-470-86657-3}}</ref>{{rp|152}} is a [[Complex number|complex-valued]] mathematical [[sequence]] which, when applied to a [[signal]], gives rise to a new signal of constant [[amplitude]]. When [[circular shift|cyclically shifted]] versions of a Zadoff–Chu sequence are imposed upon a signal the resulting set of signals detected at the receiver are [[autocorrelation|uncorrelated]] with one another.

== Description ==
Zadoff–Chu sequences exhibit the useful property that cyclically shifted versions of themselves are [[Orthogonality|orthogonal]] to one another.

A generated Zadoff–Chu sequence that has not been shifted is known as a ''root sequence''.

[[File:Zadoff Chu 7 353.png|thumb|500px|Plot of a Zadoff-Chu sequence for u=7, N=353]]

The complex value at each position ''n'' of each root Zadoff–Chu sequence parameterized by ''u'' is given by

: <math> x_u(n)=\text{exp}\left(-j\frac{\pi un(n+c_\text{f}+2q)}{N_\text{ZC}}\right), \, </math>

where

: <math> 0 \le n < N_\text{ZC}</math>,

: <math> 0 < u < N_\text{ZC}</math> and <math>\text{gcd}(N_\text{ZC},u)=1</math>,

: <math> c_\text{f} = N_\text{ZC} \mod 2</math>,

: <math> q \in \Z</math>,

: <math> N_\text{ZC} =  \text{length of sequence}</math>.

Zadoff–Chu sequences are CAZAC sequences ([[constant-amplitude zero-autocorrelation waveform]]).

Note that the special case <math> q = 0 </math> results in a Chu sequence,.<ref name="Zepernick" />{{rp|151}}  Setting <math>q \neq 0</math>  produces a sequence that is equal to the cyclically shifted version of the Chu sequence by <math> q </math>,  '''and''' '''multiplied''' by a complex, modulus 1 number, where by multiplied we mean that each element is multiplied by the same number.

== Properties of Zadoff-Chu sequences ==
1. They are [[Periodic function|periodic]] with period <math>N_\text{ZC} </math>.

:  <math> x_u ( n + N_{\text{ZC}} )= x_u(n) </math>

2. If <math>N_\text{ZC} </math> is prime, the [[discrete Fourier transform]] of a Zadoff–Chu sequence is another Zadoff–Chu sequence conjugated, scaled and time scaled.

:  <math> X_{u}[k]= x_{u}^{*}(\tilde{u}k) X_{u}[0]</math> where <math>\tilde{u}</math> is the multiplicative inverse of u modulo <math>N_\text{ZC} </math>.
<!--

3. The auto correlation of a Zadoff–Chu sequence with a cyclically shifted version of itself is zero, i.e., it is non-zero only at one instant which corresponds to the cyclic shift.

4. The [[cross correlation|cross-correlation]] between two prime length Zadoff–Chu sequences, i.e. different values of <math>u, u=u_1, u=u_2 </math>, is constant <math> 1/{\sqrt{N_\text{ZC}}} </math>, provided that <math> u_1 - u_2 </math> is relatively prime to <math> N_\text{ZC} </math>.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Popovic, B.M. |title=Generalized Chirp-Like polyphase sequences with optimum correlation properties |journal=IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=1406–9 |year=1992 |doi=10.1109/18.144727 }}</ref>

== Usages ==
Zadoff–Chu sequences are used in the [[3GPP]] [[Long Term Evolution]] (LTE) [[E-UTRA|air interface]] in the Primary Synchronization Signal (PSS), random access preamble (PRACH), uplink control channel (PUCCH), uplink traffic channel (PUSCH) and sounding reference signals (SRS).

By assigning [[orthogonal]] Zadoff–Chu sequences to each LTE [[eNodeB]] and multiplying their transmissions by their respective codes, the [[cross-correlation]] of simultaneous eNodeB transmissions is reduced, thus reducing inter-cell interference and uniquely identifying eNodeB transmissions.

Zadoff–Chu sequences are an improvement over the [[Walsh–Hadamard code]]s used in [[UMTS]] because they result in a constant-amplitude output signal, reducing the cost and complexity of the [[remote radio head|radio's power amplifier]].<ref>{{cite book |editor-first=Lingyang |editor-last=Song |editor2-first=Jia |editor2-last=Shen |title=Evolved Cellular Network Planning and Optimization for UMTS and LTE |publisher=CRC Press |location=New York |year=2011 |isbn=978-1439806500 }}</ref>
